findings.title: `answer` records the answer and restarts the deadline before delivery; if delivery fails, the worker never gets the answer and a --no-herdr rerun is refused
findings.description: answer_main calls record_answer (the answer is stored, `paused_at` is cleared and the deadline runs again) before deliver_answer. herdr() raises when HERDR_ENV != 1 (workflow/herdr.py:10), deliver_answer raises when terminals.json has no pane for the lane (line 535, whose message says 'rerun with --no-herdr'), and send-text raises when the pane is gone. In each case the command exits 1 'Blocked', but the question already counts as answered, so `answer ... --no-herdr` is then refused with 'Worker ui has no unanswered question' and never prints `claude attach`. RUNBOOK.md:56 says the opposite: 'With --no-herdr, or if the pane is gone, it prints claude attach <id>... the answer stays recorded'. WorkerQuestion covers only the successful delivery (HERDR_ENV=1 and a recorded pane).
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced in scratch: a lane with one waiting question; `python -m workflow answer RUN ui "Use B"` from a shell without HERDR_ENV prints 'Recorded the answer to question 1 of ui; its deadline runs again.' then 'Blocked: Herdr controls require a Herdr-managed caller pane', exit 1. questions.json now has answer 'Use B' and deadline.json has paused_at null. Rerunning with --no-herdr gives 'Blocked: Worker ui has no unanswered question', exit 1. The worker stays idle with no answer while its deadline runs, until it expires and the run blocks.
findings.suggested_fix: Deliver first and record only after delivery succeeds. Or, when delivery fails, catch the error and print the `claude attach <background_id>` line with the recorded answer text, then exit 0, as the RUNBOOK promises. Make --no-herdr on an already-answered latest question reprint the attach command instead of refusing. Add WorkerQuestion cases for HERDR_ENV unset and for a lane missing from terminals.json.

findings.title: A question completion is read only when the native state is idle/done, but the same loop says a turn ending in a question reports `blocked`; the test fakes only `idle`
findings.description: wait_handoffs processes `<node>.completion.json` (and so record_question) only when `row["state"] in {"idle", "done"}`. The comment a few lines above (automatic.py:194) says a native session reports `blocked` 'when its turn ended needing a human: a question, a permission prompt or a refusal'. The completion prompt tells the worker to write the question and end its turn, which is exactly that case. WorkerQuestion sets ui to 'idle' in every step, so this test data cannot catch the problem. Whether the native harness really reports `blocked` here was not verified; the in-repo comment says it does.
findings.failure_scenario: Scratch probe on the WorkerQuestion fixture with states['ui'] = 'blocked' and a 1.1.0 question completion written at t=10. wait_handoffs records only the 'needs attention in its pane' event. No ui.questions.json or ui.deadline.json is written, and at t = TIMEOUT+5 it raises 'Worker ui deadline exhausted'. `answer ui "Use B"` is refused with 'Worker ui has no unanswered question'. Nothing pauses the deadline and `answer` cannot be used.
findings.suggested_fix: Also read a completion whose status is `question` when the state is `blocked`, for example `row["state"] in {"idle", "done", "blocked"} and path.exists()` for the question branch. Parametrise WorkerQuestion over the idle and blocked native states.

findings.title: A fourth question blocks the run but exports as completion status `question` with no waiting question and no question text
findings.description: PRD 2 and 4.6 say a fourth `question` is treated as `blocked`. record_question raises before moving the file, so `<lane>.completion.json` stays with status `question`. completion_signal (export_state.py:181) serves it as status `question` and drops the `question` text, and the questions list holds three answered entries. The only trace of the block is a `controller` event. The viewer shows the lane as waiting on a question (WorkerInputs.tsx:207: 'the worker ended its turn with a question, listed below') that it never lists, and `answer` refuses it. The worker-question test (test_guardrails.py:541-546) asserts only the RuntimeError and that the file still exists, never what the run records.
findings.failure_scenario: Checked in scratch: three answered questions in ui.questions.json plus a 1.1.0 completion with status 'question' and question 'Fourth: A or B?'. completion_signal returns {'status': 'question', ..., 'falsifying_check': None, ...} and worker_questions returns three answered entries. The served inputs show a lane waiting on the operator after the controller has already stopped the workers as blocked, and the fourth question's text appears nowhere in the viewer.
findings.suggested_fix: On a fourth question, record it as blocked evidence: move the file to `<lane>.question-4.json` and write or export a completion with status `blocked` whose summary includes the question text, or map it to `blocked` in completion_signal. Extend the worker-question test to assert the exported completion status is `blocked` after the fourth question.

findings.title: No test covers the challenge failure paths; treating any challenge error as a pass still passes every test
findings.description: Constraint in controller-task.md: never launch a worker before the challenge is passed, accepted or disabled. run_challenge has six error paths: non-zero exit or is_error, a session_id mismatch (identity), schema-invalid output, a changed worktree, the deadline (TimeoutExpired), and a leftover challenge.running.json handled by challenge_gate. RUNBOOK.md:42 promises each one blocks `start` with a `blocked` event and launches no worker. The fake executable in test_guardrails always succeeds with valid output, so none of these paths runs. The scenario tests only cover passed, paused, accepted and disabled.
findings.failure_scenario: Mutation in a scratch copy of 7c5e37e: challenge_gate becomes `try: return run_challenge(runtime, 1)["status"] == "passed" except RuntimeError: return True`, so a crashed, timed-out or invalid challenge launches the workers. `python -m unittest workflow.test_guardrails` still passes (9 tests OK), and no other test module exercises the challenge.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a GuardedFeature test that makes the fake exit non-zero, then return output violating challenge.schema.json, then echo a different session_id. For each, assert `start --live` exits 1, a `challenge` `blocked` event exists, no challenge.json is written, launches() == ['challenge'], and a following `start` refuses with the 'never decided; rerun it with resume' message.

findings.title: ChallengePauses claims to prove the resumed launch used the re-pinned plan, but the assertion cannot fail
findings.description: resume_main rebuilds the runtime after the re-pin (guardrails.py:560) so the sessions that launch the workers hold the new task and decisions and bind receipts to the new plan digest. repin mutates runtime.plan in place, and export_state reads runtime.plan, so the export shows the new task even without the rebuild. FakeSessions.run builds no prompt and checks no plan digest. The assertion at lines 331-332 therefore passes whether or not the workers were launched from the re-pinned plan.
findings.failure_scenario: Mutation in a scratch copy: remove `runtime = Pipeline(directory)` at guardrails.py:560. ChallengePauses still passes (2 tests OK). A probe that wraps FakeSessions.run shows the ui session then holds the task without the edit, and its plan digest differs from plan.json. With real InteractiveSessions the worker prompt would carry the stale task and decisions, and the receipt's plan_digest (interactive.py:180) would fail the digest checks the next controller process makes (interactive.py:69/133/293).
findings.suggested_fix: Assert on what the launching session saw. Have the test's FakeSessions record `plan_digest(self.plan)` and `worker_prompt(...)` at run(), then assert the digest equals plan_digest(read_json(plan.json)) and the prompt contains the edited task line (and the edited decisions, see the next finding).

findings.title: `resume` re-reading decisions.md and the PRD is untested; removing either re-pin passes every test
findings.description: PRD 4.5 says `resume` re-reads the task files, decisions.md and the PRD from the paths pinned at prepare and updates the plan's pinned copies. ChallengePauses edits only ui-task.md, and it asserts decisions_sha256 is unchanged (line 328), which is the expected result with or without the decisions re-pin. No test edits decisions.md or the PRD before resume, so the challenge prompt, prd_sha256, challenge-inputs/ and the worker/reviewer decisions block after a resume are never checked.
findings.failure_scenario: Mutations in a scratch copy: (a) remove `plan["decisions"]["text"] = text` (line 394); (b) remove the `pin_prd` re-pin (lines 395-396). With either one, `python -m unittest workflow.test_guardrails` passes (9 tests OK). An operator who answers a P1 by editing decisions.md or the PRD and runs `resume` would rerun the challenge on the old text, possibly pause again, and the workers' prompts would carry the old decisions.
findings.suggested_fix: In ChallengePauses, edit decisions.md (add a marker) and docs/PRD.md before one resume. Assert the marker is in plan['decisions']['text'], in the last challenge prompt and in worker_prompt(); assert decisions_sha256 and prd_sha256 changed and challenge-inputs/prd.md holds the new bytes.

findings.title: `resume` handing an automatic run to the supervisor is never exercised
findings.description: After a paused automatic launch (the launch now stops at `start`, test_guardrails.py:356-372), `resume` is the only thing that restarts the automatic supervisor: `if runtime.plan.get("automatic"): supervise(directory)`. Every ChallengePauses run is prepared without --automatic, so this branch never runs in any test.
findings.failure_scenario: Mutation in a scratch copy: replace `supervise(directory)` with `pass`. `python -m unittest workflow.test_guardrails` still passes (9 tests OK). In a live automatic run, after `resume --accept-challenge "r"` the workers would start but no controller would poll their completions, verify or review; the run would stall until the operator noticed and ran `automatic --live`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a case that prepares the guarded feature with --automatic, pauses, then resumes with `workflow.automatic.supervise` patched. Assert it is called once with the run directory after the workers launch, and not called when the rerun is still paused.

findings.title: `answer` records the answer and restarts the deadline before delivery; if delivery fails, the worker never gets the answer and a --no-herdr rerun is refused
findings.description: answer_main calls record_answer (the answer is stored, `paused_at` is cleared and the deadline runs again) before deliver_answer. herdr() raises when HERDR_ENV != 1 (workflow/herdr.py:10), deliver_answer raises when terminals.json has no pane for the lane (line 535, whose message says 'rerun with --no-herdr'), and send-text raises when the pane is gone. In each case the command exits 1 'Blocked', but the question already counts as answered, so `answer ... --no-herdr` is then refused with 'Worker ui has no unanswered question' and never prints `claude attach`. RUNBOOK.md:56 says the opposite: 'With --no-herdr, or if the pane is gone, it prints claude attach <id>... the answer stays recorded'. WorkerQuestion covers only the successful delivery (HERDR_ENV=1 and a recorded pane).
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced in scratch: a lane with one waiting question; `python -m workflow answer RUN ui "Use B"` from a shell without HERDR_ENV prints 'Recorded the answer to question 1 of ui; its deadline runs again.' then 'Blocked: Herdr controls require a Herdr-managed caller pane', exit 1. questions.json now has answer 'Use B' and deadline.json has paused_at null. Rerunning with --no-herdr gives 'Blocked: Worker ui has no unanswered question', exit 1. The worker stays idle with no answer while its deadline runs, until it expires and the run blocks.
findings.suggested_fix: Deliver first and record only after delivery succeeds. Or, when delivery fails, catch the error and print the `claude attach <background_id>` line with the recorded answer text, then exit 0, as the RUNBOOK promises. Make --no-herdr on an already-answered latest question reprint the attach command instead of refusing. Add WorkerQuestion cases for HERDR_ENV unset and for a lane missing from terminals.json.

findings.title: A question completion is read only when the native state is idle/done, but the same loop says a turn ending in a question reports `blocked`; the test fakes only `idle`
findings.description: wait_handoffs processes `<node>.completion.json` (and so record_question) only when `row["state"] in {"idle", "done"}`. The comment a few lines above (automatic.py:194) says a native session reports `blocked` 'when its turn ended needing a human: a question, a permission prompt or a refusal'. The completion prompt tells the worker to write the question and end its turn, which is exactly that case. WorkerQuestion sets ui to 'idle' in every step, so this test data cannot catch the problem. Whether the native harness really reports `blocked` here was not verified; the in-repo comment says it does.
findings.failure_scenario: Scratch probe on the WorkerQuestion fixture with states['ui'] = 'blocked' and a 1.1.0 question completion written at t=10. wait_handoffs records only the 'needs attention in its pane' event. No ui.questions.json or ui.deadline.json is written, and at t = TIMEOUT+5 it raises 'Worker ui deadline exhausted'. `answer ui "Use B"` is refused with 'Worker ui has no unanswered question'. Nothing pauses the deadline and `answer` cannot be used.
findings.suggested_fix: Also read a completion whose status is `question` when the state is `blocked`, for example `row["state"] in {"idle", "done", "blocked"} and path.exists()` for the question branch. Parametrise WorkerQuestion over the idle and blocked native states.

findings.title: A fourth question blocks the run but exports as completion status `question` with no waiting question and no question text
findings.description: PRD 2 and 4.6 say a fourth `question` is treated as `blocked`. record_question raises before moving the file, so `<lane>.completion.json` stays with status `question`. completion_signal (export_state.py:181) serves it as status `question` and drops the `question` text, and the questions list holds three answered entries. The only trace of the block is a `controller` event. The viewer shows the lane as waiting on a question (WorkerInputs.tsx:207: 'the worker ended its turn with a question, listed below') that it never lists, and `answer` refuses it. The worker-question test (test_guardrails.py:541-546) asserts only the RuntimeError and that the file still exists, never what the run records.
findings.failure_scenario: Checked in scratch: three answered questions in ui.questions.json plus a 1.1.0 completion with status 'question' and question 'Fourth: A or B?'. completion_signal returns {'status': 'question', ..., 'falsifying_check': None, ...} and worker_questions returns three answered entries. The served inputs show a lane waiting on the operator after the controller has already stopped the workers as blocked, and the fourth question's text appears nowhere in the viewer.
findings.suggested_fix: On a fourth question, record it as blocked evidence: move the file to `<lane>.question-4.json` and write or export a completion with status `blocked` whose summary includes the question text, or map it to `blocked` in completion_signal. Extend the worker-question test to assert the exported completion status is `blocked` after the fourth question.

findings.title: No test covers the challenge failure paths; treating any challenge error as a pass still passes every test
findings.description: Constraint in controller-task.md: never launch a worker before the challenge is passed, accepted or disabled. run_challenge has six error paths: non-zero exit or is_error, a session_id mismatch (identity), schema-invalid output, a changed worktree, the deadline (TimeoutExpired), and a leftover challenge.running.json handled by challenge_gate. RUNBOOK.md:42 promises each one blocks `start` with a `blocked` event and launches no worker. The fake executable in test_guardrails always succeeds with valid output, so none of these paths runs. The scenario tests only cover passed, paused, accepted and disabled.
findings.failure_scenario: Mutation in a scratch copy of 7c5e37e: challenge_gate becomes `try: return run_challenge(runtime, 1)["status"] == "passed" except RuntimeError: return True`, so a crashed, timed-out or invalid challenge launches the workers. `python -m unittest workflow.test_guardrails` still passes (9 tests OK), and no other test module exercises the challenge.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a GuardedFeature test that makes the fake exit non-zero, then return output violating challenge.schema.json, then echo a different session_id. For each, assert `start --live` exits 1, a `challenge` `blocked` event exists, no challenge.json is written, launches() == ['challenge'], and a following `start` refuses with the 'never decided; rerun it with resume' message.

findings.title: ChallengePauses claims to prove the resumed launch used the re-pinned plan, but the assertion cannot fail
findings.description: resume_main rebuilds the runtime after the re-pin (guardrails.py:560) so the sessions that launch the workers hold the new task and decisions and bind receipts to the new plan digest. repin mutates runtime.plan in place, and export_state reads runtime.plan, so the export shows the new task even without the rebuild. FakeSessions.run builds no prompt and checks no plan digest. The assertion at lines 331-332 therefore passes whether or not the workers were launched from the re-pinned plan.
findings.failure_scenario: Mutation in a scratch copy: remove `runtime = Pipeline(directory)` at guardrails.py:560. ChallengePauses still passes (2 tests OK). A probe that wraps FakeSessions.run shows the ui session then holds the task without the edit, and its plan digest differs from plan.json. With real InteractiveSessions the worker prompt would carry the stale task and decisions, and the receipt's plan_digest (interactive.py:180) would fail the digest checks the next controller process makes (interactive.py:69/133/293).
findings.suggested_fix: Assert on what the launching session saw. Have the test's FakeSessions record `plan_digest(self.plan)` and `worker_prompt(...)` at run(), then assert the digest equals plan_digest(read_json(plan.json)) and the prompt contains the edited task line (and the edited decisions, see the next finding).

findings.title: `resume` re-reading decisions.md and the PRD is untested; removing either re-pin passes every test
findings.description: PRD 4.5 says `resume` re-reads the task files, decisions.md and the PRD from the paths pinned at prepare and updates the plan's pinned copies. ChallengePauses edits only ui-task.md, and it asserts decisions_sha256 is unchanged (line 328), which is the expected result with or without the decisions re-pin. No test edits decisions.md or the PRD before resume, so the challenge prompt, prd_sha256, challenge-inputs/ and the worker/reviewer decisions block after a resume are never checked.
findings.failure_scenario: Mutations in a scratch copy: (a) remove `plan["decisions"]["text"] = text` (line 394); (b) remove the `pin_prd` re-pin (lines 395-396). With either one, `python -m unittest workflow.test_guardrails` passes (9 tests OK). An operator who answers a P1 by editing decisions.md or the PRD and runs `resume` would rerun the challenge on the old text, possibly pause again, and the workers' prompts would carry the old decisions.
findings.suggested_fix: In ChallengePauses, edit decisions.md (add a marker) and docs/PRD.md before one resume. Assert the marker is in plan['decisions']['text'], in the last challenge prompt and in worker_prompt(); assert decisions_sha256 and prd_sha256 changed and challenge-inputs/prd.md holds the new bytes.

findings.title: `resume` handing an automatic run to the supervisor is never exercised
findings.description: After a paused automatic launch (the launch now stops at `start`, test_guardrails.py:356-372), `resume` is the only thing that restarts the automatic supervisor: `if runtime.plan.get("automatic"): supervise(directory)`. Every ChallengePauses run is prepared without --automatic, so this branch never runs in any test.
findings.failure_scenario: Mutation in a scratch copy: replace `supervise(directory)` with `pass`. `python -m unittest workflow.test_guardrails` still passes (9 tests OK). In a live automatic run, after `resume --accept-challenge "r"` the workers would start but no controller would poll their completions, verify or review; the run would stall until the operator noticed and ran `automatic --live`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a case that prepares the guarded feature with --automatic, pauses, then resumes with `workflow.automatic.supervise` patched. Assert it is called once with the run directory after the workers launch, and not called when the rerun is still paused.
